text:
Taylor (People Ops): Hey — need help adding a temporary dependent to benefits. Court granted temporary guardianship for my niece for ~4 months (signed 2026-02-12). I'm past open enrollment — is this a QLE? What docs/steps do I need and any deadlines?
Nina (Benefits): Yes, this qualifies as a QLE (change in household/guardianship). You have 30 days from the court order date to submit for enrollment. We'll need a legible copy of the court order/temporary guardianship, the child’s birth certificate (or proof of relationship), and SSN if available.
Jordan: Quick Q — do those docs need to be notarized originals or are scanned PDFs okay?
Nina (Benefits): Scanned PDFs are fine if they're legible. Originals/notarization not required for our internal review. If the docs are from another country, please include an English translation and any apostille if available.
Priya (Payroll): Note on payroll: premiums will be prorated based on the effective date you choose. If the effective date is retro (within the 30-day window), any retro premium will be billed on the next payroll run.
Taylor (People Ops): Effective date on the order is 2026-02-12. I’ll need the exact link to the QLE form + where to upload docs.
Nina (Benefits): Submit the QLE form and upload docs to the benefits portal. Link: https://benefits.redwood.com/qle-form (internal). Email uploads are accepted only to our secure upload endpoint or via the portal. Use this email subject when emailing (if needed):
```
Subject: QLE - Add dependent - Taylor (temporary guardian) - 2026-02-12
Attach: court_order.pdf, birth_certificate.pdf, ssn_or_note.pdf
```
Nina (Benefits): After upload, ping me here and I’ll expedite the review.
HRbot: Ticket created: HR-5421 — "QLE add dependent: Taylor" (assigned to Nina).
Priya (Payroll): Also, in the benefits portal choose "Add dependent" and enter the dependent details. If SSN isn’t available at time of submission, place "TBD" and update later — payroll needs a placeholder to process enrollment.
Max: Any implications for claims while we process? Immediate coverage?
Nina (Benefits): Medical coverage will be effective as of the chosen effective date (the court order date is acceptable). Most carriers waive waiting periods for dependents added due to a QLE, but dental/vision carriers sometimes have different rules — I’ll check with the vendor if you tell me which plans you’re on. If anything looks off, we can temporarily authorize urgent claims on a case-by-case basis while records are processed.
Taylor (People Ops): One last thing — does the child’s parent need to sign anything for our records? The court order lists temporary guardianship and signatures are on that document.
Nina (Benefits): The court order itself is sufficient. No extra parent signature required beyond what’s on the order. Please upload the docs and post "uploaded" here once done and I’ll mark it for immediate processing. :thumbsup:
